final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position to match the existing concern set. That reframing is more proportional than the original broader certification defense, but it does not satisfy the unresolved compliance predicate. Under the policy text, a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the available record says this segment is named in customer commitments. The same record also says legal disclosure review is still open. On actor-summary-only evidence, there is still no admissible exception, approval, or policy basis permitting certification despite that unresolved material weakness/disclosure issue. A caveated narrative may be more accurate than a clean certification claim, but caveating the packet is not the same as establishing policy compliance. The remaining issue is unresolved evidence, not tone or framing.
remaining_concerns: The affected clinical coding assistant segment is described as named in contractual hospital revenue-cycle commitments, which meets the policy text's materiality trigger on the present record.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so the materiality and disclosure predicate is unresolved.
No admissible approval, exception, or governing-policy basis was provided showing certification may proceed while that named-segment weakness and disclosure question remain unresolved.
Aggregate readiness passing and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not override the specific materiality rule in the policy text.
Public governance guidance about documenting limitations and post-launch monitoring is relevant to risk management but does not establish compliance with the governing certification policy.
